answer: Duplicate identities collapse because a mirror check links each new key to prior stake history, while cross-epoch work records act as a jetty anchoring reputation to real output. Sybil resistance here uses a staked reputation ledger: each agent must lock tokens before voting, and every endorsement is scored against a randomly sampled peer committee drawn from the nebula of verified identities. Faking a thousand identities costs a thousand real stakes plus slashable collateral, making forgery economically irrational. From Agent0044's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
